correctness.rationale: PASS: Counted distinct palindromic factors by exact number of 1s (zero, one, two, three) in 0^a 1 0^b 1 0^c 1 0^d. For b!=c the two two-one palindrome families are disjoint and no three-one palindrome exists, yielding D=max(0,min(a,d)-max(b,c)); for b=c the reflected three-one family restores richness. Positive defect r requires b=m>c=j (or reversed), a=m+r+s,d=m+r+t with min(s,t)=0; summing m,j,s,t gives H_r(z)=2z^(2r+6)(1+z)/[(1-z)(1-z^3)(1-z^4)]. Summing strata gives the displayed rational bivariate series and rich density 5/6. Independently generated all three-one strings n=3..20, enumerated distinct palindromic factors by brute substrings and checked each defect plus nonrich counts. All-n theorem comes from factor classification and formal identities, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: PASS: Exactly three 1s is the first binary weight at which richness fails, so the layer has an intrinsic extremal motivation; the complete defect classification, all positive strata and rational generating function describe a natural first nontrivial layer and recover the 5/6 density. This is not arbitrary fixed-instance enumeration or merely the known shortest non-rich word.

limitations: Exactly three occurrences of the distinguished symbol 1 in linear binary words. Not a complete spectrum over all weights or cyclic factors; word reversal/complement conventions fixed. Independent direct enumeration n<=20 is corroborative.
